note: CDLS6 is indeed caused by BRD4 mutations originally described by Olley et al. (2018) presenting with CdLS-like features including microcephaly, developmental delay, and facial dysmorphisms.

evidence.text: Mutations in BRD4 were identified in patients exhibiting a Cornelia de Lange-like phenotype, demonstrating overlapping features of CdLS such as developmental delay, microcephaly, and characteristic dysmorphic signs.

source.title: Non-Classic Cornelia de Lange Syndrome Due to BRD4 Gene Alterations: A Literature Review
source.quote: The heterozygous mutations in the BRD4 gene that were identified in patients with CDLS6 by Olley et al.

evidence.text: BRD4 was identified as a critical gene associated with a Cornelia de Lange-like phenotype due to functional interaction with the cohesin-loading factor NIPBL.

source.title: Confirmation of BRD4 haploinsufficiency role in Cornelia de Lange–like phenotype and delineation of a 19p13.12p13.11 gene contiguous syndrome
source.quote: Recently, BRD4 (19p13.12) was proposed as a new critical gene associated with a mild CdLS because of a similar presentation of the patients carrying point mutations and of its involvement in the NIPBL pathway.
